validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — confirmed real by multiple independent, non-GEM sources. Iran's 6th national gas trunkline (IGAT-6 / IGAT VI): NIGC announced full operation 4 July 2018 (Euro-Petrole; Caspian Barrel), Financial Tribune 2018 'construction complete', and two independent engineering/EPC-management contractors publish project pages (PEMC/pemcq.ir; the market-data profile at offshore-technology.com). Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION — correct: it is a national gas transmission trunkline (transmission, Fuel=Gas), not gathering/process/feeder and not an oil/NGL line. DUPLICATE — not a duplicate: distinct from the other IGAT rows in the roster (IGAT 1/2/3/4/7/8/10). GulfPub lists a single 'IGAT 6 | Assaluyeh -> Khuzestan | 56 in | 311 km' feature that clearly maps to this same physical pipe (1:1), not to another GEM PID. SPECS vs >=2 independent: diameter 56 in — confirmed (offshore-technology; pemcq). Length 600 km — GEM 600 corroborated by offshore-technology 'IGAT VI Expansion' (600 km) and pemcq ('more than 595 km'); GulfPub's 311 km disagrees and is treated as a partial/segment outlier, so keep 600 (tier medium, cluster 595-600). Capacity 3884.6 MMcf/d = 110 mcm/d — widely attested (Financial Tribune; secondary refs) but I could NOT verify it on a clean independent URL (Financial Tribune pages are JS-gated and failed the verifier), so the value is retained but its ref stays UNRESOLVED; note this same 3884.60 appears on IGAT 8 (P0447) — coincidence of both being ~110 mcm/d, not evidence of duplication. Start 2018 — confirmed (BOT contract July 2015, fully operational Dec 2018 / launched July 2018). ATTRIBUTION caveats: (1) operator is the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) per Euro-Petrole/Caspian Barrel; GEM's Owner1 = 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' is the parent (defensible as owner) but the operating subsidiary NIGC is more precise, and GulfPub's 'NIOC' is wrong for a domestic gas trunkline. (2) Route endpoint NAME fields on the sheet are placeholder junk ('Asia'/'Asia') while RouteAccuracy is set 'high' — the corridor is well documented (Asaluyeh -> Khuzestan, then west through Ilam/Kermanshah, feeding Iraq at Shalamcheh) but the terminus field should be populated with a real place.

fills.researcher_notes: Replaces rotted GECF ASB-2024 PDF (404, and a generic stat bulletin that never named IGAT-6). NIGC declared IGAT-6 fully operational 4 July 2018; still operating.
Fully launched July 2018; Financial Tribune / Wikipedia give Dec 2018 as first-operational. 2018 confirmed. BOT contract signed July 2015.
56-inch max diameter confirmed by two independent sources (offshore-technology market data 'maximum diameter of 56 inches'; PEMC contractor page '56 inches').

600 km corroborated by offshore-technology's 'IGAT VI Expansion' (600 km) and PEMC ('more than 595 km'). The base-line offshore-technology profile also cites a 493 km onshore figure, and GulfPub lists 311 km — both read as partial/segment figures. Sources cluster at 595-600 km, so keep 600 (tier medium given the segment-length ambiguity).

Start Asaluyeh (Bushehr) -> Khuzestan corridor confirmed by offshore-technology (originates at Bushehr, ends in Khuzestan) and PEMC (passes through Khuzestan, Ilam, Kermanshah; 'between Shalamcheh and Kermanshah'). Province-level start/end is high confidence; the specific end city 'Khorramshahr' is medium — the line's Iraq-export tie-in is at Shalamcheh (adjacent to Khorramshahr), while some contractor sources describe the trunk continuing north to Kermanshah. Endpoint city retained as Khorramshahr but flagged.

Operated by the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), which is a subsidiary of the Ministry of Petroleum, so the Ministry-of-Petroleum owner value is defensible as parent. Recommend adding NIGC as the operator for precision. GulfPub's operator 'NIOC' is incorrect for a domestic gas trunkline (NIGC, not NIOC, handles gas transmission).

routes.corridor_desc: Runs from the South Pars gas hub at Asaluyeh on the Bushehr coast north-westward into Khūzestān Province, serving Khuzestan and feeding gas westward and to Iraq via the Shalamcheh border (adjacent to Khorramshahr). Contractor sources (PEMC) describe the trunk passing through Khūzestān, Ilam and Kermanshah provinces ('between Shalamcheh and Kermanshah'), implying the corridor may continue north to Kermanshah beyond the Khorramshahr/Shalamcheh delivery area. Corridor is well bounded province-by-province; the exact terminus is ambiguous (Khuzestan/Shalamcheh vs Kermanshah).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent sources: offshore-technology (Bushehr origin -> Khuzestan end) and PEMC (Shalamcheh-Kermanshah, passes Khuzestan/Ilam/Kermanshah). Coordinates are the known locations of Asaluyeh, Ahvaz, Khorramshahr and the Shalamcheh border crossing (not fabricated; no route-file geometry was invented). The sheet's Start/End name fields currently read 'Asia'/'Asia' (placeholder) despite RouteAccuracy='high' — recommend populating with the named endpoints above. Existing high RouteAccuracy is plausible for the corridor but the terminus should be pinned (Shalamcheh/Khuzestan vs Kermanshah).

summary: IGAT 6 (P0445) confirmed real, correctly classified gas transmission trunk, not a duplicate; caveats: placeholder route endpoint fields ('Asia'), operator is NIGC (not NIOC/Ministry), length 600 km kept over GulfPub's 311 km outlier, capacity 3884.6 MMcf/d ref UNRESOLVED.
